text: {"cases":[{"id":"C06","status":"conflict","pairs":[["C06-A","C06-B"]],"reason":"Both statements describe the same signed final revision 3 of report Q7, the same region, and the same period, April 2025. C06-A says that revision records exactly 420 completed jobs. C06-B and its republished copies say it records exactly 390. The two figures cannot both be right."},{"id":"C12","status":"insufficient","pairs":[],"reason":"C12-A reports 1,000 completed responses from first-time customers to survey S9 in June 2025. C12-B reports 2,000 completed responses to the June 2025 customer survey, but does not say which survey version was used or which respondent groups were included. C12-B does not state whether its 2,000 covers the same population as C12-A's first-time respondents."},{"id":"C05","status":"conflict","pairs":[["C05-A","C05-B"]],"reason":"Both statements cover the same rule, R5 effective 2025-06-01, and an applicant exactly 18 years old who meets all other requirements. C05-A says that applicant is eligible; C05-B says that applicant is ineligible. These are direct opposites."},{"id":"C03","status":"conflict","pairs":[["C03-A","C03-B"]],"reason":"Both statements give the final settled total refund for invoice INV-204 on 2025-02-18, inclusive of adjustments. C03-A gives USD 138.00 and C03-B gives USD 183.00. The same dollar total cannot be both."},{"id":"C07","status":"compatible","pairs":[],"reason":"These are separate agencies' baseline values. NASA's figure (about 1.2 C) is measured against its 1951–1980 baseline, while NOAA's figure (1.18 C) is measured against the 20th-century average. They come from different analyses with different reference periods, so they are not the same measurement."},{"id":"C08","status":"compatible","pairs":[],"reason":"The two statements cover different periods. C08-A gives 138 refunds in March 2025, and C08-B gives 183 refunds in April 2025. Different periods is not a conflict."},{"id":"C10","status":"compatible","pairs":[],"reason":"Both statements describe the same change, from 8% to 10%. C10-A states it as an increase of 2 percentage points, and C10-B states it as a 25% relative increase measured against the initial 8%. These are two valid ways to express the same change, not contradictory claims."},{"id":"C02","status":"conflict","pairs":[["C02-A","C02-B"]],"reason":"Both statements cover release Orion 4.2 under its default configuration, and both describe the audit's findings. C02-A says unsigned extensions are not permitted to execute, with no exception. C02-B says they are permitted to execute, with no exception. These cannot both hold."},{"id":"C11","status":"insufficient","pairs":[],"reason":"C11-A gives a 10% refund rate for March 2025. C11-B gives 12% but does not specify an observation period, and the record notes that no date is supplied. The two statements cannot be compared because it is unknown whether they cover the same period."},{"id":"C01","status":"conflict","pairs":[["C01-A","C01-B"]],"reason":"Both cover NASA's 2023 anomaly against the 1951–1980 baseline. C01-A says the anomaly was about 1.2 C, with 2.1 F as the Fahrenheit equivalent. C01-B and its copies claim 2.1 degrees Celsius and explicitly deny that the number is Fahrenheit. 2.1 C is not a valid conversion of 1.2 C."},{"id":"C04","status":"conflict","pairs":[["C04-A","C04-B"]],"reason":"Both statements give the final audit results for batch B17 before any repair or retest, covering the same 37 included units. C04-A says all 37 units passed the insulation test, with zero failures. C04-B says unit B17-09, one of those 37 units, failed. These cannot both hold."},{"id":"C09","status":"compatible","pairs":[],"reason":"The two statements describe the same sensor T3 checkpoint and the same sample. 32 degrees Fahrenheit converts exactly to 0 degrees Celsius, and C09-B is explicitly presented as that conversion."}]}
